findings.body: That image's `kc.sh build` rejects the unknown feature and the Docker build exits unsuccessfully, breaking the existing ability to use this version-parameterized Dockerfile with older releases.
findings.failure_mode: Building a custom image against an older supported base terminates during the `RUN kc.sh build` layer.
findings.impact: That image's `kc.sh build` rejects the unknown feature and the Docker build exits unsuccessfully, breaking the existing ability to use this version-parameterized Dockerfile with older releases.
findings.root_cause: A feature available only in the new release is passed unconditionally even though the base image version remains caller-selectable.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the extra feature argument configurable and only set it for supporting versions, or explicitly constrain and validate `VERSION` to a release that contains `rolling-updates`.
findings.title: Custom-image builds now fail for older selectable Keycloak versions
findings.trigger: The Dockerfile's `VERSION` or `IMAGE` build argument selects a Keycloak image from before the `rolling-updates` feature was introduced.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch at line 5 of Dockerfile-custom-image adds '--features=rolling-updates' unconditionally, but the Dockerfile accepts VERSION as a build arg (line 2) allowing older Keycloak images. Older images lack this feature, causing 'kc.sh build' to fail with unknown feature error. This is a concrete backward compatibility issue introduced by the patch.

pr.title: Feature flag: rolling-updates

raw_findings.body: The Operator still selects and executes its update strategy instead of rejecting or failing the CR, so the preview functionality remains usable while its newly introduced feature flag is disabled.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The documented feature boundary is bypassed in Operator deployments.
raw_findings.impact: The Operator still selects and executes its update strategy instead of rejecting or failing the CR, so the preview functionality remains usable while its newly introduced feature flag is disabled.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch registers the feature and checks it in the update-compatibility CLI, but adds no corresponding check to the Operator's update-strategy selection or reconciliation path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Before honoring `spec.update`, validate the CR's effective feature configuration and report a failed status when `rolling-updates` is not enabled; retain the legacy behavior for CRs that do not opt into the update configuration.
raw_findings.title: The rolling-updates feature is not enforced by the Operator
raw_findings.trigger: A Keycloak CR configures `spec.update.strategy`, such as `Recreate`, but does not enable `rolling-updates` in `spec.features.enabled`.

raw_findings.body: That image's `kc.sh build` rejects the unknown feature and the Docker build exits unsuccessfully, breaking the existing ability to use this version-parameterized Dockerfile with older releases.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Building a custom image against an older supported base terminates during the `RUN kc.sh build` layer.
raw_findings.impact: That image's `kc.sh build` rejects the unknown feature and the Docker build exits unsuccessfully, breaking the existing ability to use this version-parameterized Dockerfile with older releases.
raw_findings.root_cause: A feature available only in the new release is passed unconditionally even though the base image version remains caller-selectable.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make the extra feature argument configurable and only set it for supporting versions, or explicitly constrain and validate `VERSION` to a release that contains `rolling-updates`.
raw_findings.title: Custom-image builds now fail for older selectable Keycloak versions
raw_findings.trigger: The Dockerfile's `VERSION` or `IMAGE` build argument selects a Keycloak image from before the `rolling-updates` feature was introduced.

raw_findings.body: Every explicit-strategy test enables the feature, while no test submits the same update configuration without it; consequently the suite passes even though the Operator currently permits the disabled feature path.
raw_findings.failure_mode: CI cannot detect that update strategies are accepted without the required preview feature.
raw_findings.impact: Every explicit-strategy test enables the feature, while no test submits the same update configuration without it; consequently the suite passes even though the Operator currently permits the disabled feature path.
raw_findings.root_cause: The test setup adds only the successful opt-in configuration and introduces no negative feature-gating scenario.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add an integration test that sets `spec.update.strategy` without enabling `rolling-updates` and asserts the expected failed reconciliation/status, alongside the existing feature-enabled cases.
raw_findings.title: Operator tests do not cover rejection when the feature is disabled
raw_findings.trigger: The Operator ignores or later regresses the required feature check for a CR containing an explicit update strategy.

finding.title: The rolling-updates feature is not enforced by the Operator
finding.trigger: A Keycloak CR configures `spec.update.strategy`, such as `Recreate`, but does not enable `rolling-updates` in `spec.features.enabled`.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that the Operator lacks enforcement of the rolling-updates feature is speculative. The patch adds the feature flag and the CLI commands check it, but there is no evidence in the provided context that the Operator's UpgradeLogicFactory should reject CRs when the feature is disabled. The UpgradeLogicFactory code shows it simply selects strategy based on UpdateSpec without any documented requirement to validate feature enablement. The finding assumes a missing check without concrete evidence this is a bug rather than intended design.

finding.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage observation, not a defect in the patch. The test code at line 115 enables the feature when updateStrategy is non-null, which is the intended test scenario. The absence of a negative test case is a test gap suggestion, not a bug introduced by this patch. Test coverage gaps are stylistic/quality concerns rather than functional defects.
